prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures an indoor bakery or store layout where a multi-tiered glass display case sits below and directly in front of the camera wearer within arm's reach (roughly 0.3 to 1.0 metres away) in frames 1 to 4, positioned against a wall on the right (about 0.4 to 1.2 metres away), before the wearer turns right and retreats in frame 5 to reveal a hallway and back wall roughly 2 to 4 metres ahead. Inside the display case, cylindrical cakes and smaller pastries sit on tiered shelves separated by about 0.15 to 0.3 metres vertically and horizontally, with the upper and right edges of the black frame brightest as the wearer leans closer in frames 2 through 4 (within 0.3 to 0.5 metres) before turning away in frame 5 where the display case edge remains very close on the far left. No other standing people are present in the scene, and the camera wearer's own hand reaching into the lower shelf in frame 3 is mostly occluded by the case structure and indistinct in depth. The depth map clearly reveals the continuous 3D surface inclination of the adjacent wall and the receding depth plane of the shelves and hallway floor even under heavy motion blur in frame 5 that makes RGB details hard to judge. However, the map is unreliable on the transparent glass panels, wire racks, and dark reflective frame in frames 3 and 4, where it either flattens the interior cakes into the glass surface or assigns erroneously far (black) values to dark structural regions.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map attempts to isolate foreground structures across the 5 frames as the camera wearer leans down toward the display case (frames 1 to 4, roughly 0.3 to 1.0 metres away) and then turns away toward a wider room (frame 5, roughly 2 to 4 metres deep), while showing no other people in the actual RGB scene. Although the masks delineate the angled spatial footprint of the display case top in frame 1 (extending from the lower-left at about 1.0 metre to the lower-right within 0.5 metres), the lower pastry shelf in frame 2, the entire close-up display interior in frame 3, and the receding wall plane in frame 5 (about 1.5 to 3.0 metres ahead between the left display case and right doorway), every single class label is wrong. Specifically, the map misclassifies the black display case top as a 'cell phone' in frame 1, the lower shelf of pastries as a 'keyboard' (and 'remote') in frame 2, the entire glass case and cakes as a 'person' in frame 3, nothing at all in frame 4, and the flat poster-covered wall as a 'refrigerator' in frame 5. While the sharp mask boundaries in frames 1, 2, and 5 help separate the tilted display case planes and the vertical wall edge from the dark floor and adjacent fixtures despite perspective distortion and motion blur in RGB, the map is highly unreliable for identifying objects or true occlusions, completely missing the individual cakes, the actual refrigerated display on the far left of frame 5, and the wearer's reaching hand at the bottom of frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost entirely empty across the 5-frame sequence, confirming that no other people are standing or facing the camera wearer in the room. In frame 1, it renders a spurious yellow body skeleton in the lower-left corner over the pastry shelf (roughly 0.8 to 1.2 metres away and below eye level) and a spurious magenta hand skeleton over the black display case top on the right (within arm's reach at about 0.5 metres), neither of which corresponds to an actual person or hand in the RGB image. Meanwhile, in frame 3, when the camera wearer's own hand or arm actually enters the bottom-left foreground within 0.3 to 0.5 metres to reach into the lower shelf (partly occluded by the case frame and cut off by the bottom image border), the pose map fails to detect it at all. Frames 2, 3, 4, and 5 remain completely black as the camera wearer leans toward the case and then turns right, providing no usable spatial information beyond the absence of full-body subjects and demonstrating high unreliability through both false-positive detections on bakery fixtures in frame 1 and a false negative on the egocentric hand in frame 3.
